Mr. ___ is a ___ man with complicated medical

with systolic CHF with EF around 30%, with recent finding of

ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Dyspnea: 
# Acute on chronic systolic CHF exacerbation: LVEF ___
Patient presenting with worsening SOB, volume overload on exam, 
and elevated BNP. CXR indicative of pulmonary edema. Cultures 
negative. Patient's symptoms improved s/p BIPAP and Lasix. He 
does have a significant hx of CAD. ACS is or stent stenosis is 
unlikely given EKG and enzymes were negative. Patient has had a 
5 month decline with worsening of EF on ECHO, which may possibly 
have been precipitated by a missed MI. His acute exacerbation 
was thought to be precipitated by a viral GI illness. On 
presentation, patient was given Lasix IV boluses for diuresis.  
On first day of admission, he appeared to have poor perfusion 
and cool extremities, low UOP concerning for cardiogenic shock.  
He was started on a Dobutamine gtt and Lasix gtt which he 
responded well to.  He was able to wean from the Dobutamine drip 
and ultimately transitioned to PO Torsemide.  During 
hospitalization, he had a persantine MIBI which demonstrated 
normal myocardial perfusion and EF of 32%.  Patient was 
discharged on Torsemide 40mg daily for maintenance dose and 
Spironolactone 12.5mg daily.  He was continued on Losartan 100mg 
daily.  He was ultimately started on Carvedilol in place of 
Metoprolol and was tolerating Carvedilol 3.125mg BID at time of 
discharge.  For afterload reduction, patient was initiated on 
Isordil and Hydralazine.  He was subsequently transitioned to 
Imdur and continued on Hydralazine at time of discharge.  Dry 
weight (Discharge weight) 125.5kg.
 
# Cardiogenic shock:
Following admission, patient became increasingly cool on exam 
with low urine output, and rising lactate. Likely precipitated 
by decompensated CHF. Improved with dobutamine gtt. Echo 
demonstrating elevated RV pressures affecting LV function, 
severe PAH, several focal wall motion deficits. Subsequently 
weaned off dobutamine as above. 

# Acute Kidney Injury:  Patient had an acute worsening in his 
renal function initially in the setting of cardiogenic shock and 
renal venous congestion.  Subsequently recovered but then had 
recurrent ___ (peak of 2.5) thought to be related to slight 
overdiuresis. Creatinine at discharge was 1.6 and baseline 
closer to 1.3.

# CAD s/p CABG: Had been on on ASA 325 at home, converted to ASA 
81mg daily given no indication for ASA 325mg daily. 

# Concern for renal cell carcinoma: Patient has a recent 
radiographic diagnosis of a renal mass, and was referred to 
hem/onc and urology at ___. Patient had staging CT scans done 
prior to admission showing no evidence of metastatic disease.  
Prior to discharge, communicated with Dr. ___ Dr. ___ to 
help coordinate care and follow up plan for patient's renal 
mass. 

CHRONIC ISSUES:
#GERD: Continued home omeprazole.
 
#BPH: continued home tamsulosin.

# Acute on chronic systolic CHF exacerbation: LVEF ___

does have a significant hx of CAD. ACS is or stent stenosis is

presentation, patient was given Lasix IV boluses for diuresis.  
On first day of admission, he appeared to have poor perfusion 
and cool extremities, low UOP concerning for cardiogenic shock.

responded well to.  He was able to wean from the Dobutamine drip 
and ultimately transitioned to PO Torsemide.  During 
hospitalization, he had a persantine MIBI which demonstrated 
normal myocardial perfusion and EF of 32%.  Patient was 
discharged on Torsemide 40mg daily for maintenance dose and

daily.  He was ultimately started on Carvedilol in place of 
Metoprolol and was tolerating Carvedilol 3.125mg BID at time of 
discharge.  For afterload reduction, patient was initiated on 
Isordil and Hydralazine.  He was subsequently transitioned to 
Imdur and continued on Hydralazine at time of discharge.  Dry 
weight (Discharge weight) 125.5kg.

Following admission, patient became increasingly cool on exam 
with low urine output, and rising lactate. Likely precipitated 
by decompensated CHF. Improved with dobutamine gtt. Echo 
demonstrating elevated RV pressures affecting LV function, 
severe PAH, several focal wall motion deficits. Subsequently 
weaned off dobutamine as above.
